title: A conformance scenario: two testees, a and b, and the steps the runner drives them through.

name.description: Unique within its layer; the test's name.

replaces.description: The gate this scenario took the place of, for the record.

needs.description: Layers and features the steps ask for, the union over both sides: what the steps of each side ask is derived from them and held against that side's testee alone, and the runner refuses a file whose needs differ from the union, so the declaration stays what places the scenario in a profile and nothing more.

mirror.description: Run the scenario as written and again with a and b exchanged, so that a scenario whose sides differ — one serves, one dials — holds each language in each seat of every pairing.

table.description: A path under conformance/, e.g. tables/frames.json; its `rows` array.

as.description: The name a row is bound to: $<as>.<member> refers into it.

where.description: Rows are kept whose members equal these.

foreach.description: Expands the scenario once per row of a table, each named name[i].

on.description: Which testee takes the op; runner for a pair.* op, which the runner expands into the testees' ops from what each answered hello with, so that whichever side can listen does.

args.description: The op's arguments; a string value may be a placeholder.

bind.description: A string binds the answer's handle (or, when the answer is a scalar, the answer); an object binds each named member of the answer to a name.

expect.description: The answer's ok value must match this, with placeholders.

expect_error.description: The op must answer with an error matching this: its code, and whatever members an error of that op carries. Beside expect, the step holds whichever kind the answer is to the one written for it.

absent.description: This text appears nowhere in the answer's JSON.

present.description: This text appears somewhere in the answer's JSON.

until.description: Stop repeating at the first answer of this kind — or, with match, at the first answer whose expect and assert hold, which is how a step waits for what the far side has yet to do; the step then holds its expectations against the last answer.
